**STEP 1 - Scene:** A plain snack or side of pale, cubed tofu on a white square plate, photographed from above at a slight angle. No sauce, oil, or other food is visible.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white square plate is about 22 cm across. Its area is roughly 22 x 22 ≈ 480 cm². Individual tofu cubes measure about 2 cm per side, which I used to size the pieces.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Firm tofu, cut into roughly 2 cm cubes, about 20 pieces, piled in the centre of the plate.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The tofu pile covers about 18% of the plate, roughly 85 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Footprint of about 85 cm² x about 1.8 cm typical pile height ≈ 150 ml gross volume.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Tofu is dense, so I used a bulk density of 0.9 g/ml. 150 ml x 0.9 ≈ 135 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Firm tofu is about 144 kcal per 100 g. 135 g x 1.44 ≈ 194 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 20 cubes of firm tofu at roughly 6–7 g each is consistent with about 135 g. This is a visual estimate, and the true weight could easily be 100–170 g.
